"Let's make a deal. Don't ignore my concerns, and I won't badger you about your decisions. Agreed?"
column2: "You know, a few years ago I would have stormed off and left you to look after your own messes. I guess I've grown."
column3: "The less we say to each other right now, the better."

column1: "Best if I keep my thoughts to myself right now. I don't want to argue."
column2: "I can suffer fools, dull blades, bland food, and miserable weather. But you … you are testing my patience."
column3: "I agreed to work with you, not flatter you. If you want false admiration, it will cost extra."

column1: "I'm worried about the sort of choices you seem to make. I'm not sure we're after the same things."
column2: "Will you be quiet? You're driving me to drink!"
column3: "This is a business arrangement, nothing more. I said I'd work with you. I didn't say I liked you."

column1: Let's talk about something else. (Returns to Greetings)
